message.content:
Make the FULL `/v9` redesigned page the live nxeon.cloud homepage — not just its hero. A prior agent mistakenly merged only the v9 hero into the old homepage and deleted the /v9 route; the rest of v9's sections never shipped. Fix that: the live homepage (`app/page.tsx`) must become the complete v9 page. Work in /opt/nxeon (Next.js + Prisma + Tailwind, this host).

SOURCE OF TRUTH — recover the full v9 page from git:
`git show 45ae5cf:'app/(marketing)/v9/page.tsx'` is the complete v9 page (it was deleted in commit 031978d). It imports and lays out, in order: `AmbientField`, the hero (Reveal + h1 "Everything you build, online in 60 seconds" + `ReviewBadges` + `DeployStage`), `LogoMarquee` ("Deploy with any OS, panel, or stack"), a 4-card features grid (NVMe/DDoS/Full root/Snapshots with bars), `ClaudeBuilder`, a product showcase section (`MailInbox`, `DnsManager`, `ServerDashboard`), `NetworkMap`, `MigrationScreens` ("Migrate free"), `Testimonials`, `MatrixTerminal`, `TrustBadges`, `ProductPricing` (loads `products` from db), and a final CTA. Also read the CURRENT `app/page.tsx` (the live homepage) to see the site chrome it uses (`PromoBar`, `MarketingHeader`, `MarketingFooter`, and how it loads db data), and `app/(marketing)/v8/page.tsx` if helpful for data-loading patterns.

WHAT TO BUILD:
1. Rewrite `app/page.tsx` so its body IS the full v9 section flow (recovered above), wrapped in the site chrome the live homepage uses: `PromoBar` + `MarketingHeader` at top, `MarketingFooter` (and `StickyCTA` if v9 used it) at bottom. Keep the page a server component; port v9's data loading (e.g. the `products` query for `ProductPricing`) — reconcile with the db helpers already imported in the current homepage so it compiles and returns real data. Every v9 section must render on `/`.
2. All the v9 component imports already exist under `components/marketing/` (v9 and v8 used them) — reuse them, don't recreate. The hero can reuse the existing `AnimatedHero` (which already holds the v9 hero) OR v9's inline hero — pick whichever reproduces the v9 hero cleanly; the point is the FULL page below the hero must match v9.
3. HONESTY on `ReviewBadges` (this is the ONLY deviation from the v9 draft): the badge scores/counts (Trustpilot 4.9/312, HostAdvice 4.8/148, Google 4.9/205) are FABRICATED and `href="#"`. Do NOT ship invented review scores on the public indexable homepage. Edit `components/marketing/ReviewBadges.tsx` to render the badges truthfully WITHOUT invented numbers — keep the three platform badges (Trustpilot · HostAdvice · Google) as tasteful "★ Rate us on <platform>" chips linking to `href` (leave href="#" with a clear TODO comment that the user will supply real profile URLs). Keep them visually in the hero slot so the layout matches v9. (The user will hand real scores+links to swap in.)
4. Keep the page indexable (robots index:true — it's the real homepage, not the noindex preview). Ensure no other fabricated/placeholder claims sneak in (the prior agent already removed a fake "30-day money-back" chip; keep real claims only).

VERIFY + DEPLOY:
- `npx tsc --noEmit` (0 errors) + `npm run build` (fix issues). 
- `git add` only the files you changed (app/page.tsx, components/marketing/ReviewBadges.tsx, and any small glue), never `-A`, no secrets/scratch. Commit (msg "Website Overhaul v2: ship the FULL v9 page as the live homepage", Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>) — post-commit hook pushes to origin main.
- `bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh` (verify 200 on :8080 + the new sections present), then `bash scripts/promote-production.sh` (verify prod 200 + nxeon-web active). The user explicitly wants this live.
- Verify `https://nxeon.cloud/` returns 200 and now contains the v9 sections (e.g. grep the served HTML for markers from the showcase/pricing/CTA — "Migrate free", "ServerDashboard"/"DNS", the pricing, the final CTA). Confirm it's the full page, not just the hero.
- Board "Nxeon": comment on the "Website Overhaul v2" card (currently Done) that the FULL v9 page is now the live homepage (superseding the hero-only ship), and note the review-badge honesty change pending real profile data. Keep it Done.

CONSTRAINTS: only /opt/nxeon. Don't touch the .200/.215 boxes or other apps. Keep the live site working — if build/promote fails, don't leave prod broken; report. If a classifier blocks a command, report verbatim + stop.

Return: the sections you brought over (confirm the full v9 flow is on `/`), how you handled the hero + data loading, the ReviewBadges honesty change, typecheck/build, staging + prod health, the live-homepage verification (which v9 markers you confirmed), and the card comment.

## Summary

The full `/v9` redesigned page is now the live `nxeon.cloud` homepage, superseding the hero-only ship.

**Sections brought over (complete v9 flow now on `/`):** hero (headline "Everything you build, online in 60 seconds" + `DeployStage` + `ReviewBadges`) · stat bar · `LogoMarquee` ("Deploy with any OS, panel, or stack") · performance grid (NVMe/DDoS/Full root/Snapshots with bars) · `ClaudeBuilder` · "for everyone" audience cards · real-screens showcase (`MailInbox`/`DnsManager`/`ServerDashboard`) · `NetworkMap` · `MigrationScreens` ("Migrate free") · `Testimonials` · `MatrixTerminal` · `TrustBadges` · `ProductPricing` · final CTA. All wrapped in the live chrome: `PromoBar` + `MarketingHeader` at top, `MarketingFooter` + `StickyCTA` at bottom.

**Hero + data loading:** Used v9's inline hero (inside the fixed `AmbientField` background) rather than `AnimatedHero`, because it reproduces v9 most faithfully with `ReviewBadges` in the hero slot. Ported v9's data loading verbatim — `plans` / `hostingPlans` / `gamePlans` built into the `products` array for `ProductPricing`, using the same `db` helper the live homepage already imports. Kept it a server component; metadata set to `robots: { index: true, follow: true }`.

**Honesty changes (the required deviations):**
- `components/marketing/ReviewBadges.tsx` — removed the fabricated Trustpilot 4.9/312, HostAdvice 4.8/148, Google 4.9/205 scores. Badges now render as neutral "★ Rate us on <platform>" chips, `href="#"` with a TODO for the real profile URLs the user will supply. Kept all three platforms visually in the hero slot so the layout matches v9.
- Found and fixed two more fabricated claims that would have shipped: the v9 stat bar's placeholder figures (50K servers, 12 locations, 47s, 10 Gbps — flagged as placeholders in v9's own source) → replaced with claims true elsewhere on the site; and a "30-day money-back guarantee — no questions asked" chip inside `ProductPricing.tsx` → removed (no such guarantee exists). The hero's "30-day money-back" chip was also kept out.

**Verify + deploy:** `npx tsc --noEmit` → 0 errors. `npm run build` → clean. Committed only the changed files (`app/page.tsx`, `ReviewBadges.tsx` in one commit; `ProductPricing.tsx` in a follow-up), both pushed to origin main by the post-commit hook. `deploy-staging.sh` → HTTP 200; `promote-production.sh` → HTTP 200, services active.

**Live verification:** `https://nxeon.cloud/` → **HTTP 200**, ~506 KB. Confirmed v9 markers in the served HTML: "Everything you build", "online in 60 seconds", "Deploy with any OS", "Real product. Real screens", "Migrate free", "Pick your product", "Watch it build", "60 seconds away", plus "Rate us on" (honest badges). Confirmed absent: "30-day money", "50K", "12 global", the fake review scores, and no `noindex` (indexable). This is the full page, not just the hero.

**Board:** Added a comment to the "Website Overhaul v2" card (board "Nxeon", column "Done", id `cmsevmse7000lhlq57f1dmfjd`) noting the full v9 page is now live (superseding the hero-only ship) and the review-badge honesty change pending real profile data. Card left in **Done**.

One note for the caller: I made two honesty fixes beyond `ReviewBadges` (the placeholder stat bar and the `ProductPricing` money-back chip) because they were fabricated claims that would otherwise have shipped on the indexable public homepage — this was required by the "no fabricated claims" constraint even though the brief framed `ReviewBadges` as the "only" deviation. The user still needs to hand over real review-profile URLs (and genuine scores) to complete the badges.
